item.title: The Liberty Bell
item.description: A 2,080-pound cast bronze bell of Pennsylvania State House provenance, retired from active ringing duty after acquiring a crack that, depending on the source, came from routine use, cold weather, or simply trying too hard.

item.title: Lock, Padlock Brass
item.description: A security device characterized by its robust brass construction and notable heft, often serving both utilitarian and decorative roles on outdoor fences.

item.title: Thiccc Ferris Wheel
item.description: A towering amusement device characterized by its impressive radial girth, often seen silhouetted against the skyline with a circumference that suggests a profound commitment to rotational leisure.

item.title: Concrete Bunker, Soviet
item.description: A monumental construct of reinforced concrete, typically characterized by its formidable thickness and unyielding presence; esp. one observed in stark contrast against placid bodies of water.

item.title: Thiccc Antenna Array
item.description: A towering structure sporting an abundance of antennae, each vying for attention like a telecommunications colossus, particularly imposing when viewed in silhouette against the skyline.

item.title: Pizza, Deep Dish
item.description: A culinary construct of formidable depth, characterized by a thick crust that forms a vessel for an abundance of toppings; esp. one observed from above, in a state of savory contemplation.

item.title: Saucer, Satellite Dish
item.description: A parabolic reflector engineered to receive or transmit data signals, often characterized by an exaggerated depth and breadth that challenges conventional suburban landscapes.

item.title: Adobe, Architectural
item.description: A construction style renowned for its formidable mass and earthen hues, characterized by thick walls of sun-dried brick. Often observed in Southwestern settings, where it invites a spell of winter warmth.

item.title: Slab, Granite Countertop
item.description: A substantial slab of polished stone, often occupying pride of place in a kitchen, distinguished by its imperious thickness and lustrous surface.

item.title: Chair, Beanbag Oversized
item.description: A seating apparatus of notable volume and soft constitution, characterized by an expansive profile that eclipses standard furniture dimensions; esp. one observed from behind, where its generous silhouette defies spatial modesty.

item.title: Cake, Wedding Three-Tier
item.description: A confectionary monument of stacked indulgence, typically composed of three graduated layers, each encased in fondant and supported by internal engineering. Esp. one viewed in raking light, where shadows deepen its architectural intrigue.

item.title: Trophy, Stanley Cup
item.description: A championship trophy of prodigious magnitude, renowned for its imposing height and tiered design, traditionally awarded in professional hockey. Its presence in the trophy case is less a display and more a gravitational center.

item.title: Brick, Firebrick Furnace
item.description: A specially designed refractory brick, robust in thermal resilience, used to line high-temperature enclosures such as furnaces and kilns; esp. one perceived as gravitationally significant when viewed astern in raking light.

item.title: Crane, Tower Construction
item.description: A towering fixture of engineering prowess, designed to reach vertiginous heights while supporting substantial loads; especially when viewed against a skyline, its silhouette exemplifies thiccc industrial elegance.

item.title: Eiffel Tower, Iron Lady
item.description: A wrought iron structure of unparalleled posterior breadth, famed for its steadfast refusal to be anything but thiccc; often admired astern against a tumultuous sky.

item.title: Beam, Steel I-Beam
item.description: A structural member of unapologetic heft, typically employed in bridges and buildings, characterized by its cross-sectional shape resembling the letter 'I'. Esp. notable when viewed from a distance, where its thicccness defies casual description.

item.title: Column, Doric Greek
item.description: A structural pillar of disciplined stoutness, characterized by its fluted shaft and austere capital, often observed in ancient temples where its presence remains unchallenged.

item.title: Water Tower, Municipal Steel
item.description: An elevated storage structure for potable water, characterized by its substantial girth and top-heavy silhouette, often nestled within urban landscapes like a sentinel of hydration.

item.title: Cinder Block, Concrete
item.description: A rectangular unit of precast concrete, primarily employed in the construction of load-bearing walls, characterized by its uncompromising heft and voids that suggest a robustness beyond the sum of its parts.

item.title: Cathedral, Concrete Brutalist
item.description: A monumental ecclesiastical structure characterized by its unapologetically bulky concrete forms and stark geometric lines; typically possessing a cavernous interior that suggests a sanctuary for contemplation and echoes.

item.title: Fire Hydrant
item.description: An outdoor fixture of conspicuous girth, typically found along urban sidewalks, designed for high-volume water discharge in emergency situations; particularly striking when viewed astern, defying casual description.

item.title: Vault Door, Bank
item.description: A security barrier of formidable rotundity, typically installed to guard the inner sanctum of financial institutions, esp. when viewed astern, in raking light.

item.title: Globe, Library Floor Model
item.description: A spherical representation of Earth, often observed on library floors, notable for its substantial diameter and formidable heft, requiring a table of equally impressive foundation to remain stationary.

item.title: Boulder, Glacial Erratic
item.description: A substantial rock formation, often resting incongruously upon a landscape, relocated by ancient glacial activity, notable for its commanding presence when viewed astern in natural light.

item.title: Silo, Grain Concrete
item.description: A towering agricultural structure characterized by its substantial cylindrical form and ability to outshine any pastoral landscape with its commanding presence.

item.title: Hoover Dam
item.description: A concrete arch-gravity dam spanning the Black Canyon of the Colorado River, completed 1936; 726 feet from foundation to crest, 660 feet of base thickness tapering to 45 feet at the crown.

item.title: Basilica, San Pedro
item.description: A monumental ecclesiastical structure in Vatican City, notable for its expansive nave and an apse that seems to embrace the horizon; its thiccc columns and domes defy casual description.

item.title: Ferris Wheel, London Eye
item.description: A monumental observation wheel situated on the South Bank of the River Thames, noted for its unparalleled rotundity and panoramic dominion over the skyline.

item.title: Pipe, Industrial Stack
item.description: A towering cylinder of engineered steel, designed for the expulsion of industrial emissions at a formidable height, often characterized by its unapologetic girth when viewed from any direction.

item.title: Bell, Cathedral
item.description: A resonant structure of considerable mass, often found suspended in lofty ecclesiastical towers, its substantial profile best appreciated when viewed from a respectful distance.
